about:
Design Warehouse has operated as a Santa Fe, New Mexico retail destination since 1981. Located the store has served as a long-standing source for contemporary furniture, lighting, and home accessories. The business remains independently owned, though no founder names are disclosed in public records.

The company operates a brick-and-mortar showroom offering a curated selection of furniture, lamps, and home accessories. Its product range includes wardrobe systems such as the Garden Party line in Oblivion and White finishes. The business ships orders via USPS Ground for smaller items and common carrier for larger furniture pieces, with shipping costs tiered by order value: $10 for orders up to $49, $20 for orders $50–$99, and free shipping on orders over $100. All web orders and furniture sales are final.

The store serves residential customers in the Santa Fe area and ships to the other 47 states. Its clientele includes local residents and out-of-state buyers seeking contemporary home furnishings. A 2019 review in Local Flavor Magazine described the showroom as "the place in town to come for the most beautiful, artfully designed furniture, lamps and home accessories."

Design Warehouse emphasizes personal service, encouraging customers to call for quotes and support. The company validates free parking for one hour at its off-site lot and maintains a phone-first approach to customer communication.

old_description: Detroit Woodworking specializes in custom residential woodworking, collaborating with homeowners, architects, and designers to create handcrafted cabinetry, intricate moldings, and custom furniture with exceptional attention to detail. Serving Grosse Pointe and Metro Detroit, we blend traditional and modern design using premium materials to craft durable, inviting spaces while ensuring a seamless experience from consultation to installation.
about:
Detroit Woodworking is a family-owned millwork and cabinetry shop based in Roseville, Michigan, serving the metro Detroit area and shipping nationwide. The company was founded on a commitment to traditional craftsmanship combined with modern manufacturing technology, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed.

The shop operates a state-of-the-art production facility equipped with CNC machining, laser engraving, and professional finishing systems. Its capabilities span custom cabinetry, architectural millwork, custom doors, live-edge furniture, conference tables, healthcare and educational casework, specialty fabrication, and prototype or one-off projects. The team handles projects from design engineering and 3D rendering through material selection, manufacturing, finishing, and installation, with typical production timelines of eight to twelve weeks.

Detroit Woodworking serves a diverse client base including homeowners, architects, designers, developers, and corporations across industries such as hospitality, restaurants, retail, healthcare, education, multi-family housing, residential construction, and corporate environments. Projects range from luxury residential kitchens and built-ins to commercial fixtures, displays, and large-scale replicable millwork programs.

The company differentiates itself through a design-build approach that integrates dedicated project management, white-glove delivery, climate-controlled storage, and a limited lifetime warranty on all custom cabinetry and millwork. As one of the few Detroit-area shops with a state-of-the-art laser engraving machine, it can incorporate intricate detailing into both residential and commercial pieces.

old_description: Regardless of whether you live with Type 1 Diabetes or Type 2 Diabetes one thing remains…when you don’t have your supplies it is stressful and can be dangerous. We understand the critical nature of insulin pumps, CGMs and glucometers and it impacts everything we do.
about:
Diabetic Equipment and Supplies operates from Johnston, Iowa, with an additional location in Indiana, serving customers across 26 states. The company focuses exclusively on providing diabetes management equipment and supplies to individuals living with Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes.

The business distributes insulin pumps, continuous glucose monitors (CGMs), glucometers, and related supplies. Its service model assigns each patient a dedicated Patient Care Coordinator who manages the entire process from initial order through ongoing resupply. Coordinators handle insurance verification and billing for Medicaid, Medicare, and commercial plans, and the company waives shipping fees on resupply orders.

Customers include patients directly, as well as endocrinologists, healthcare providers, diabetes educators, and other medical professionals who refer or coordinate care. The coordinators work solely with diabetes products and insurance processes, providing specialized support rather than general medical supply distribution.

The company emphasizes relationship-based service: patients work with a single point of contact, avoid automated phone systems, and receive proactive outreach for resupply via phone, text, or email with personal follow-up if needed.

name: Dickson Industries Inc
old_description: Since 1946, the Dickson name has guaranteed integrity, innovation, and a commitment to excellence. Generations of customers have relied on Dickson to deliver on our promise.
about:
Dickson Industries Inc. traces its roots to April 30, 1946, when Allied Manufacturing Co. was founded at 115 SW 8th Street in Des Moines, Iowa, to produce cotton stockinette for meat packers. Arthur D. Dickson, initially hired as a sales engineer, purchased the company in the 1960s, renamed it Dickson Industries, and moved operations to the Interstate Bakery Building at 325 SW 5th Street. The business remains a third‑generation, family‑owned enterprise; Arthur W. Dickson became president in 1972, and his son David Dickson assumed the role in 2014.

Today the company operates 216 high‑tech knitting machines and full cut‑and‑sew facilities across roughly 50,000 square feet, employing 49 people. Its product lines include custom knit fabrics, garments, and textile products: freezerwear and insulated apparel (Cold Room Coat, quilted vests), food‑processing nets and sleeves (DeliKnit, RoastKnit), industrial filtration covers (DrainKnit), and medical textiles such as PPE, lab coats, surgical drapes, and orthopedic fabrics. An in‑house embroidery division, Dickson Designs, adds custom branding.

Dickson serves food processors, medical and healthcare providers, industrial filtration OEMs, hospitality and footwear brands, and geotextile markets. Customers range from national meat‑packing plants to hospitals and international distributors, with the company’s centralized Midwest location enabling quick delivery across the United States.

The Dickson name emphasizes integrity, innovation, and a commitment to excellence backed by SQF certification (achieved in 2018) for food‑safety assurance. The company highlights confidential custom development, thorough testing, cost containment, and responsive service—including emergency shipping—as core differentiators.

name: DigitTron Technologies Inc
old_description: Our electronics manufacturing expertise and processes will get your products to market faster.
about:
DigitTron Technologies Inc. is an electronic component manufacturer based in Shawnee, Kansas, a suburb of Kansas City. The company was founded in 2011 and became a subsidiary of Pivot International in 2016, expanding its global reach with parent company offices in the UK, Hong Kong, and manufacturing facilities in Asia. Co-founder Victor Turnbaugh serves as general manager, a team that includes industrial designers, engineers, technicians, and assemblers.

The company operates a 13,800-square-foot, humidity-controlled facility where it provides surface-mount assembly, conventional through-hole assembly, X-ray inspection, box-build integration, potting, and conformal coating. Staff are trained to IPC workmanship standards, and the shop handles both small prototype runs and full production volumes without minimum order restrictions.

DigitTron serves customers in telecommunications, medical equipment, agriculture, transportation, lighting, and general industrial markets. Its client base spans hundreds of companies across the United States, ranging from start-ups to established OEMs.

The firm emphasizes a one-source model that combines design, assembly, and test under one roof, backed by rigorous quality control aligned with ANSI/J-STD-001, ANSI/J-STD-002, and IPC-A-610D standards. Management highlights cost management through smart design and on-time delivery as key differentiators.

name: Dixon Power Systems
old_description: After 17 years of owning an automotive repair shop, Jon Dixon needed a new challenge and had a growing interest in Renewable Energy. With the encouragement of his wife Holly, the business was launched. Dixon Power Systems began as a part-time business in the spring of 1999 and expanded to full time in January of 2005.
about:
Dixon Power Systems is based in Lincoln, Nebraska. The company traces its roots to 1999 when Jon Dixon, after 17 years running an automotive repair shop, launched a part-time venture in renewable energy with encouragement from his wife Holly. The operation became full-time in January 2005. The business remains a privately held, husband-and-wife enterprise.

The firm designs and installs custom solar photovoltaic and wind turbine systems for on-grid, off-grid, and backup-power applications. It also operates a storefront where customers can purchase pre-engineered system packages and components. Services include site assessment, system engineering, procurement, installation, and commissioning. No facility size or headcount figures are publicly disclosed.

Clients range from homeowners and farms to small businesses seeking independence from utility power or reliable backup electricity. Typical projects serve customers in remote locations without grid access, those pursuing environmental goals, and others wanting resilience against outages. The company has supplied systems for residential, agricultural, and light-commercial installations across Nebraska and neighboring states.

Jon Dixon’s background in automotive mechanical and electrical systems informed the company’s hands-on, problem-solving approach. He has pursued continuing education with industry experts and serves on the board of Nebraskans for Solar. The founders frame their mission around energy independence, emphasizing user-friendly designs that address each site’s unique constraints.

name: Drake Plastics Ltd. Co.
old_description: The science behind Drake’s state-of-the-art injection molding operation assures exceptional quality and consistency in molded parts. When critical tolerances and other features are impractical or impossible to achieve with injection molding alone, we can deploy our precision machining capabilities to provide hybrid molded/machined part solutions to meet the specifications required.
about:
Drake Plastics Ltd. Co. operates from Cypress, Texas, where it was founded in March 1996 by Steve Quance. The company began when Quance, then an advanced products manager at a major stock-shape supplier, recognized that niche grades of Torlon® PAI were being neglected by large producers focused on high-volume output. A catalyst arrived when Atlantic Research Corporation needed glass-reinforced Torlon 5030 for the Javelin missile program and its existing supplier discontinued the product. Quance launched Drake to fill that gap, personally investing in specialized extrusion equipment and building a team around the technical demands of ultra high-performance polymers.

Today the company extrudes, injection molds, and precision machines a range of ultra high-performance polymers—including Torlon PAI, PEEK, Ryton R-4 PPS, AvaSpire PAEK, and Ultem PEI—into stock shapes, molded parts, and machined components. Its Cypress facility is described as the largest in the world dedicated to processing these materials, and it offers hybrid molded/machined solutions when tolerances exceed what molding alone can achieve. The operation also provides in-house CT inspection, CMM inspection, mechanical testing, re-curing, annealing, priming, coating, and laser engraving.

Drake serves aerospace and defense programs (notably the Javelin missile), OEMs, government agencies, universities, distributors, and fabricators worldwide. Sales offices in Germany, France, and Taiwan support global customers. The company’s stock shapes are supplied to machine shops globally, while its molded and machined parts go into applications such as electrical components, fluid handling, transportation, and oil and gas equipment.

The business was built on producing what larger suppliers could not or would not: niche grades in efficient sizes that minimize machining waste. Quance’s vision combined technical intuition with a commitment to long-term supply assurance, exemplified by the development of Drake 4200 PAI after Solvay discontinued Torlon 4200 resin. The company maintains AS9100D and ISO 9001:2015 certification and reports on-time delivery of 98% or better.
